# Legacy reference archive

**Retired designs. Full spoilers. Not part of the current museum.**

[Read the full puzzle and solution catalogue](puzzles-and-solutions.md).

Two earlier projects were recovered. They are preserved separately because they represent different directions:

| Prototype | Source snapshot | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A / Later point-and-click opening | `7883e0aa63053e9ff4e7d711269c362000306c62` | Three exhibit rooms, five division paintings, one sculpture, two combined murals, four food rebuses, a final map meta-puzzle; nine response records |
| B / Earlier 3D museum (formerly Modern Art) | `81c759b4db1a68555a6fa346586d323bd94d5976` | Forty rooms, fifteen locks, color/sound/form/time galleries, twelve-object audit, six redaction lessons, dispatch plate, word square, optional routes, and narrative/future notes |

The combined catalogue includes exact answers, explanatory reasoning, original clue text, complete original author-atlas content, and a supplement with every redaction sheet's exact text and a verified solution. Raw content, logic, and artwork specifications are retained in `source/`; SHA-256 checksums and provenance are recorded in [source-manifest.json](source-manifest.json).

The supplied shared-chat URL could not be retrieved. This archive is grounded in recovered project files, not reconstructed conversation claims. It is complete for those recovered content snapshots; unrecorded conversation-only concepts cannot be certified as exhaustive. Original atlas links refer to the old prototype's site structure; follow the original live project for its interactive atlas.

Original sites: [three-room opening](https://puzzle-pieces-museum.johnmoore2048.chatgpt.site) and [earlier 3D museum](https://modern-art.johnmoore2048.chatgpt.site). Access to the older site follows its original audience setting; archiving did not change it.

Nothing in this directory is imported by the new game runtime. The procedural classical sculpture renderer was adapted separately as decorative geometry; it carries no inherited puzzle behavior. To reuse a puzzle, create a current proposal and explicitly document the adoption.
